title: Mexican military captures cartel leader Fausto Isidro Meza-Flores in Sinaloa
seoTitle: Mexican forces capture cartel leader El Chapo Isidro
dek: Mexican forces apprehended cartel leader Fausto Isidro Meza-Flores in Guasave following a military operation supported by US intelligence. The arrest triggered armed clashes that resulted in at least 11 deaths.
happened: On 20 November, Mexican military forces conducted a special operation in Guasave, Sinaloa, to apprehend Fausto Isidro Meza-Flores, an alleged cartel leader and FBI most-wanted fugitive. According to the Mexican Defence Ministry, the operation involved elite forces who used "stealth and surprise" to surround a residence. Upon entry, security forces were met with gunfire and explosives from suspected cartel members. The ensuing firefight lasted through the night and spread across the city, causing civilians to flee public spaces, including a baseball stadium. By 21 November, the Mexican Defence Ministry confirmed that four soldiers and seven alleged cartel gunmen had died in the conflict. Eight additional suspects were detained during the operation. Meza-Flores, along with two other alleged associates, was transported to Mexico City via air force plane. Following the arrest, the US Consulate General in Hermosillo issued a security alert regarding reports of vehicle fires and road blockades in several Sinaloa municipalities. By 21 November, authorities reported that the situation in the region had reached a state of "tense calm."

sides.says: The ministry stated that the operation was carried out by "elite military forces" with US intelligence support. They confirmed the deaths of four soldiers and seven attackers, noting that the force entered the target location after being attacked with "gunfire and explosives."

sides.who: US Department of Justice and FBI
sides.says: FBI Director Kash Patel confirmed the capture of Meza-Flores, describing him as a key figure in a network smuggling narcotics into the US. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin stated the arrest demonstrates the "outstanding strength and reach of the Homeland Security Task Force."

next: The detained individuals have been transferred to Mexico City to face prosecution. US and Mexican authorities continue to monitor the security situation in Sinaloa amid concerns regarding potential retaliatory violence from cartel factions.
summary: Mexican military forces captured Fausto Isidro Meza-Flores, a high-ranking cartel leader and FBI most-wanted fugitive, during a raid in Guasave, Sinaloa, on 20 November. The operation, supported by US intelligence, triggered significant armed clashes between security forces and cartel members, resulting in at least 11 deaths, including four soldiers. Meza-Flores, accused of leading a transnational criminal organisation involved in drug trafficking, was moved to Mexico City. The arrest prompted security alerts across Sinaloa due to reports of road blockades and vehicle fires, as experts warn of potential further instability in the region.
